subject: Life Skills
title: Stopping a Dripping Faucet
description: A short lesson to help you apply Stopping a Dripping Faucet.

hook.text: One drip per second wastes over 3,000 gallons per year. That's enough for 180 showers.

buildup.text: Faucets drip because internal washers or cartridges wear down from constant use and mineral buildup.

discovery.text: Compression faucets use rubber washers. A worn washer is almost always the culprit in older models.

twist.text: Modern cartridge faucets use ceramic discs. They drip less often but cost more to replace.

climax.text: Turn off water supply, remove the handle, replace the washer or cartridge, and reassemble. Done.

punchline.text: A five-dollar washer silences a year of dripping.

quiz.question: What usually causes a compression faucet to drip?
options: High water pressure in the pipes
Loose pipe connections under the sink
